title: Employee Engagement Survey
description: Anonymous, about 10 minutes. Think about the last three months of your work when you answer.

elements.name: anonymityNotice
elements.html: Your responses are anonymous. We do not collect your name or email address. Results are reported only for groups large enough that no individual can be identified, and written comments are shared without any details that point to their author.

elements.name: typicalWeek
elements.title: How often is each of these true in a typical week?

rows.text: When two requests compete for my time, it's clear which one comes first.
I can finish a task without waiting days for an approval or an answer.
I get a few uninterrupted hours to concentrate on my own tasks.
I choose how to approach an assignment without needing sign-off on every step.
The meetings I attend end with a decision or an agreed next step.

elements.name: meetingShare
elements.title: Roughly what share of your working week goes to meetings and calls?

elements.name: meetingShareFeeling
elements.title: How do you feel about that amount?

elements.name: teamPractices
elements.title: To what extent does each statement describe your team?

rows.text: People bring up their own mistakes in meetings so others can learn from them.
Newer or junior colleagues openly question proposals from senior people.
Requests we send to other departments get a response within a reasonable time.
We hear the reasons behind decisions that change our work, not just the outcome.
Decisions that affect us are made without long delays.
Ideas from people at every level have changed how things are done here.

elements.name: crossTeamFriction
elements.title: What slows down work between teams? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Nobody is sure who owns a task
Information is spread across too many tools
Too many people are involved in each decision
Different time zones or working hours

elements.name: recentCheckIns
elements.title: Think about your last few one-on-ones or check-ins with your manager. Which of these happened?

choices.text: We talked about more than status updates
My manager asked what was getting in my way
I got a concrete suggestion about a specific piece of my work
We agreed on something I could drop or postpone
A concern I raised earlier was followed up

elements.name: hasRegularCheckIns
elements.title: Do you have a recurring one-on-one with your manager?

elements.name: badNewsEase
elements.title: How easy is it to bring bad news or a problem to your manager?

elements.name: rampUpTime
elements.title: When you joined, how long did it take before you could handle routine tasks without asking for help?

choices.text: I joined too long ago to say

elements.name: careerMobility
elements.title: How true is each statement for you?

rows.text: People can switch to another team or role here without leaving the company first.
In the past year I was given at least one assignment I had never done before.
I could explain to a new colleague what it takes to be promoted here.
I understand how my pay is decided.

elements.name: energyAfterWork
elements.title: At the end of a typical workday, how much energy do you have left for life outside work?

elements.name: afterHoursMessages
elements.title: How often do you handle work messages in the evening, on weekends, or while on leave?

elements.name: leaveTaken
elements.title: In the last 12 months, did you take all the leave you had planned?

choices.text: No, because there was too much to do

elements.name: adviceToFriend
elements.title: A friend with your skills asks whether they should apply here. What would you tell them?

choices.text: Apply, but here are the downsides

elements.name: externalJobSearch
elements.title: Have you looked at job openings at other organizations in the last three months?

elements.name: worthProtecting
elements.title: What about working here should stay the same as the organization changes?

elements.name: fixByNextQuarter
elements.title: If you could fix one thing by next quarter, what would it be?

pages.name: aboutYou
pages.title: About You
pages.description: These questions are optional. They let us compare results between groups without identifying anyone.

elements.name: department
elements.title: Which area do you work in?

elements.name: tenure
elements.title: How long have you worked here?

elements.name: managesOthers
elements.title: Do you manage other people?

completedHtml:
Thank you for sharing your views!

Your anonymous responses have been recorded. Once the survey closes, we will publish the combined results and the steps we plan to take.
